stem: (Select TWO.) Marlowe Freight packages one module as a single file in an AWS object-storage bucket. Later an engineer edits the address in the `module` block to point at a newer file. Which two statements about this setup are accurate?

choices.text: A source that points at a plain folder of loose `.tf` objects works the same way as one that points at a packaged file
The object has to be an archive, for example a `.zip` or `.tar.gz` file
The address has to begin with `./` because the file is fetched to local disk first
`terraform plan` fetches the newer file by itself, because sources are evaluated at plan time
After the edit, `terraform init` has to run again before the new code is installed

rationale: For an S3 source the object must be an archive, and the address uses the `s3::` prefix. Changing the `source` argument requires another `terraform init`, because modules are installed at initialization. Loose `.tf` objects are not a supported shape for this kind of source, which expects one archive object. A leading `./` marks a local path to files already on disk, not a packaged file in a bucket. Plan does not fetch module code; sourcing happens at install time, not at plan time.
